title: Microsoft Teams: Copilot in channels provides channel-wide context
summary: Microsoft Teams is adding a channel-level Copilot feature allowing users to ask questions and summarize all posts and replies in a channel. Public preview starts December 2026 worldwide, with no action required. Copilot responses will include source citations and be available on Teams desktop and mobile.
body:
[What and why]

We are introducing a channel-level entry point for Copilot in Microsoft Teams. This enhancement allows users to ask questions and summarize conversations across posts and replies within a channel, rather than a single thread. This enhancement will be available in Microsoft Teams and Teams mobile.

[Rollout schedule]

- Public Preview (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by the end of December 2026.- General Availability (Worldwide): We will publish a separate announcement once we've determined a rollout schedule for General Availability.[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

- Users of Copilot in Microsoft Teams channels.Platforms and services

- Copilot- Microsoft Teams- Microsoft Teams mobileWhat will happen

- Users can open Copilot from the top-right corner of any Teams channel, ask questions, and generate summaries based on the most recent posts and replies in a channel, rather than a single thread.

- Copilot responses will include citations that link directly to the source posts or replies.[Action required and recommendations]

No additional action is required.

[Compliance considerations]

Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?

- Yes. This change introduces a new way for users to interact with generative AI in Microsoft Teams by allowing Copilot to answer questions and summarize the most recent posts and replies in a channel.
